implementation_notes: rspec-mocks provides the recording double directly: invitation = spy('invitation') records every message automatically, a partial double created with allow(obj).to receive(:msg) (optionally .and_call_original) records calls to a real object, and the assertion happens after the fact with expect(obj).to have_received(:msg).with(...). What replaces the classic spy class is the framework's double plus the have_received matcher; the docs warn that have_received(...).with(...) cannot see arguments mutated after they were recorded.
code_sketch:
mailer = spy('mailer')
OrderService.new(mailer).place(order)     # real SUT code runs

expect(mailer).to have_received(:send).with('bob@example.com', body)
pitfalls: have_received(...).with(...) compares against the recorded snapshot, so arguments mutated after the call fail the assertion (documented limitation).
allow(...).to receive without and_call_original or a configured return answers nil, so the SUT may take a different branch than production.
Doubles reset between examples, but objects stubbed in before(:all) or in shared context can leak wrapped methods into later examples - prefer per-example setup.
